A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Fourier-linear-operator learning problem and DFT-based estimator despite the changed title. The complete main texts, equations, figures and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated theoretical material.

before.justification: V1 presents theoretical bounds, propositions and proofs. Neither its main text nor Appendices A–D reports original experimental or simulation outcomes.

after.justification: V2 Section 4 and Figures 1–3 report original synthetic-data experiments measuring testing error as sample size, Fourier truncation and training-grid resolution vary.

M1.justification: The Fourier parametrization, DFT-based least-squares objective, truncation parameter K and coefficient constraint remain unchanged between v1 Section 4.2 and v2 Section 3.2. Projected SGD is newly documented as an implementation of the retained optimization problem.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates no datasets. V2 introduces empirical coverage using two-dimensional Gaussian random fields and noisy outputs from a random Fourier linear operator, including evaluation at higher resolution than training. The introductory Poisson-to-heat-equation replacement is motivational, not an evaluated task change.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical comparisons against competing methods. V2 Figures 1–3 evaluate only the proposed estimator; cited FDA and neural-operator methods are not experimental baselines.

E3.justification: V2 introduces three experimental protocols: varying sample size with N=64 and K=32; varying K with N=128 and 500 training samples; and varying N from 1 to 512 with K=N/2 and testing on a 512×512 grid. It defines a normalized squared-L2 testing-error metric evaluated on 100 test samples.

E4.justification: V2 adds sensitivity studies targeting statistical, truncation and discretization errors through sample-size, mode-count and grid-resolution sweeps. These controlled diagnostic analyses, presented in Sections 4.1–4.3, have no counterpart in v1.

E5.justification: V2 Section 4.1 first reports five independent runs, with Figure 1 displaying mean testing error and standard-deviation shading. This uncertainty reporting is limited: Section 4.2 explicitly omits error bands. V1 contains no empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 add empirical error curves absent from v1. Sections 4.1–4.3 report approximate endpoint errors of 6×10^-4 at 500 training samples, 7.9×10^-4 at K=64, and 6×10^-4 at N=512, respectively. These are newly reported results under distinct settings, not improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: The main bounds, assumptions, propositions and appendix proofs are retained after relocation and renumbering. A local mathematical correction appears in the FDA discussion: v2 Section 3.1.1 places the cross-covariance operator before the covariance pseudoinverse, whereas v1 Section 4.1.1 placed the pseudoinverse on the left.

C1.justification: The central agnostic-learning and three-error upper/lower-bound claims remain unchanged. V2 Section 1.3 explicitly presents the full-resolution discretization guarantee as formalizing multiresolution generalization, while v1 discusses formalizing that phenomenon mainly through future work in Section 5.

C2.justification: V2 Section 3.3 adds substantive discussion of the proof decomposition's applicability to nonlinear classes and cautions that controlling DFT error need not control trained-operator error with non-smooth activations such as ReLU. Section 4 also introduces interpretations of the experimental sweeps as separating the three errors.

D1.justification: V2 supplies the first experimental implementation recipe: Gaussian input and noise covariances, coefficients sampled uniformly from (-2,2), FFT/IFFT data generation, Nyquist truncation, and projected SGD enforcing coefficient magnitudes at most 2. V1 supplies estimator equations without these implementation details. Learning rates, optimization budgets and code access remain unspecified.

R1.justification: V2 adds Liu et al. (2024), Liu et al. (2025), and Golowich et al. (2018), connecting its analysis to additional operator-learning theory and width-independent neural-network bounds. It removes Boullé and Townsend (2023). The principal comparisons with FNO theory and FDA remain.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes and edits the exposition: it changes the title, rewrites the introduction, replaces the motivating PDE example, condenses preliminaries and FDA discussion, and adds a proof-technique overview. V1's formal Fourier-operator Section 3 moves to v2 Appendix A, restructuring the main narrative and appendices.

P2.justification: V2 adds three quantitative plots where v1 has no figures or tables. They display testing error against sample size, truncation mode and grid size, including a mean/standard-deviation legend in Figure 1. Numerous equations are also reformatted between displayed and inline presentation.

improvement.justification: The reorganized exposition and new proof overview make the retained theory easier to follow, while Figures 1–3 provide concrete numerical illustrations with some variability reporting. The gain is limited: the principal bounds and proofs are unchanged, optimizer details remain incomplete, and Figure 3 varies K=N/2 alongside N, preventing a clean separation of discretization and truncation effects.
